issues.legal_issue: The provision deeming a Hindu undivided family’s land to belong to one landowner operated from the date expressly specified for the amendment, and its reference to “this Act” referred to the amending Act rather than the principal Act.
material_facts: A joint Hindu family owning agricultural land executed a registered partition before the date on which the new family-land provision was deemed to take effect, and the partition was entered in the mutation register.
In determining surplus land, the authorities treated the family as one unit and disregarded the partition.
It was undisputed that the separate holdings were within the permissible limit if the partition was taken into account.
issues.conclusion: The Court held that the new provision operated from the date specified in the amending Act, not from the commencement of the principal Act. The partition was therefore to be taken into account, and the impugned orders were quashed.
issues.legal_principle: Sections 1(2) and 7 of the Pepsu Tenancy and Agricultural Lands (Amendment and Validation) Act, 1962, read together, expressly deemed the provision inserted by section 7—section 32-KK of the principal Act—to have come into force on 30 October 1956. In that context, “this Act” in section 32-KK referred to the amending Act, not the principal Act. Although an incorporated provision ordinarily uses “this Act” to refer to the principal Act, the express commencement provision made that construction impermissible. A statute must be read as a whole and harmoniously, and the Court could not treat the express commencement provision as enacted by oversight. Section 32-KK’s treatment of family partitions as dispositions operated alongside section 32-FF of the principal Act, which restricted the effect of certain dispositions made after 21 August 1956. The Court also applied the principle that retrospective operation must not be extended beyond what the legislature expressly or by necessary implication provided.

predicates.surplus_land_determination: An authority was determining whether agricultural land held by a family exceeded the applicable permissible limit.
predicates.family_partition_completed_before_amende: The family completed its partition before the amended rule governing family-owned land took effect.
predicates.partition_recorded: The family registered the partition and made corresponding entries in the land records.

issues.definition: When an authority determines surplus agricultural land and a family completed and recorded its partition before the amended rule took effect, the partition is considered in the surplus assessment.
